headline: Sarfraz Maredia, who runs Uber's autonomous mobility and delivery business, is leaving the company on 16 November after more than 12 years.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a senior departure from Uber's self-driving effort, confirmed by Uber, with no change of plan announced.
importance_line: Riders and delivery customers should see little immediate change since Uber says its focus remains scaling driverless vehicles in more cities, but the exit adds to turnover in a unit whose partnerships have stayed limited in scale, and Uber has not named a successor beyond splitting his duties.
source: Bloomberg, as relayed by Transport Topics
summary: Bloomberg reported the departure, and Transport Topics, citing an Uber spokesperson, adds that Sarfraz Maredia, Uber's global head of autonomous mobility and delivery, will leave on 16 November after more than 12 years at the company to take a top executive role at an undisclosed company outside transportation. His duties will be split between two Uber executives, Samarth Kejriwal, a senior director who oversees driverless-vehicle operations, and Aaron Emrich, head of autonomous delivery, and Transport Topics counts his exit as the latest in a string of departures from the unit in a year when Uber's partnerships with Alphabet's Waymo and Serve Robotics unravelled.
notes: Bloomberg is behind a bot check (about 470 characters of text only); text read at Transport Topics, whose headline matches Bloomberg's and was published after it, though Transport Topics does not name Bloomberg in its text.
